question: A new local government in Elche led by the PP-VOX coalition was formed on 17 June 2023. On 8 September 2023, the new local government suspended the granting of building permits for 24 solar power plants, potentially preventing the creation of 500 jobs and EUR 100 million in investment.

A written question was submitted on 13 October 2023, to which the Commission replied on 30 November 2023 saying that it was not in a position to make a comprehensive assessment of the decisions in question and their environmental impact in particular, and cited EU legislation.

Under the legislation cited by the Commission, Regulation (EU) 2022/2577 lays down a framework to accelerate the deployment of renewable energy and boost the REPowerEU plan. Furthermore, Commission working document SWD(2022)0149, linked to Recommendation C(2022)3219, calls for faster permit-granting procedures for renewable energy projects.
In view of the above: Does the Commission believe that the municipal government’s decision is consistent and compatible with EU renewable energy objectives and the above-mentioned documents?
answer: Member States have a primary responsibility to monitor the application of the relevant provisions and to take the necessary steps for enforcement. Therefore, the Commission does not have sufficient information to be able to answer the question.

The Commission is supporting Member States in transposing and implementing the relevant EU legislation — the 2018/2001 Renewable Energy Directive (1), amending 2023/2413 (2) and the 2022/2577 Council Regulation to accelerate the deployment of renewable energy (3).

The assessment of the transposition of the 2018 Renewable Energy Directive is still ongoing and there are open infringements against most Member States, including Spain (4). The amending Directive entered into force in November 2023.

It gives Member States 18 months to transpose most of its provisions and until July 2024 for some provisions related to permitting for renewables, after which transposition will be assessed. The regulation is directly applicable and its provisions may be invoked before the national authorities, including the courts, for the cases which fall within the scope of the regulation.
Directive (EU) 2018/2001 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 December 2018 on the promotion of the use of energy from renewable sources, OJ L 328, 21.12.2018.

Directive (EU) 2023/2413 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 18 October 2023 amending Directive (EU) 2018/2001, Regulation (EU) 2018/1999 and Directive 98/70/EC as regards the promotion of energy from renewable sources, and repealing Council Directive (EU) 2015/652, OJ L 2023/2413, 31.10.2023.
